**Landing + anchors (read on `origin/main` @ `603cab8`, not a worktree):** all three drifts are live —
1. `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx:349` still reads `## The one gate, three entry points`, and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:458` links the `#the-one-gate-three-entry-points` anchor — the paired-edit constraint is real (renaming the heading alone breaks the inbound link).
2. `validating-metadata.mdx:471` transcript reads `Running author-time rules (26)...` while `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` holds **38** top-level entries on main (counted, not quoted).
3. `cli.mdx:473` still lists `deprecated visibility aliases`; `visibility-alias-deprecated` is retired — live code greps only hit changesets/CHANGELOG (`visibility-alias-deprecated-retired.md`), no live rule.

**Routing rationale:** the fix lands entirely in the two hand-written gate-docs pages; they document the metadata authoring/contract gate (`AUTHORING_RULES`, `os lint` — `packages/lint`), i.e. tooling that revolves around the spec contract ⇒ `domain:spec-tooling` per the #5469 split criterion. Direct precedent: #7442 (same file, same gate table) ran as `domain:spec-tooling`.

**Dedup:** local sweep over all open issues in the three repos for `cli.mdx` / `validating-metadata` / `author-time rules` — no overlapping card (only this one; falsified the zero-hit with a known-present neighbour term). #7442 is closed via PR #7458 and deliberately excluded these three.

**Release grading:** no `target:*` — docs/display class (a mis-counted heading, a stale quoted transcript, one stale report line); nobody is blocked today, same grading family as #7307.

| 1 | heading is stale | `validating-metadata.mdx:349` — `## The one gate, three entry points` ✅ |

⚠️ **Reading 2 is sharper than the card recorded it.** The inbound reference is not only a URL anchor — the **link text** is also "The one gate, three entry points". So the rename is a **three-site coordinated edit** (heading, anchor fragment, link text), and getting two of three right leaves either a broken link or a link whose text contradicts its destination. This is exactly why #7442 declined to rename inside a single-file surface.

**ACCEPTED** — PR #7483, two files, +4/−5, one commit as ruled. `skip-changeset` applied at accept time; `mergeable_state` `clean`; undrafted and armed.

All three fixes verified on the branch by content, not by the report's say-so: heading `## The one gate, four doors`, `cli.mdx:458` carrying **both** the new anchor fragment and the matching link text, `Running author-time rules (38)`, the retired item gone, and **zero** residual `the-one-gate-three-entry-points` anywhere under `content/`.

## The heading choice was the dev's call and it is better than the one I would have made

I left A1 open and warned that "four entry points" was probably also wrong. The answer — **"four doors"** — is argued from the section's own text rather than from taste: the section introduces the fourth as *"There is a fourth door, and it is not a command"*, the sentence under the heading enumerates the three **commands**, and "door" is already the noun the section uses for the superset. It also disposed of the objection I raised: the later *"that door is not one of four — it is the only one"* is a **perspective note about one author's reachable surface**, not a competing count, so it stays true under the new heading.

## The count was right for a reason I had not measured

My dispatch said 38 as a PM assumption to falsify. It survived — but the dev found the **right reason**, which is not the one I had: that transcript line is printed by `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:117` as `authoringRulesFor('validate').length`, **not** `AUTHORING_RULES.length`.

```
AUTHORING_RULES.length        = 38
authoringRulesFor('validate') = 38   ← what this transcript prints
authoringRulesFor('lint')     = 35
```

They coincide today only because every entry currently runs on `validate`. An `os lint` transcript would have to say **35**. That is the ㊽ shape one layer in: not "is the number stale" but "**which quantity is this line even printing**".

## ⚠️ It falsified my patrol criterion, and the correction is load-bearing

I wrote that the docs-link gate was "the one gate that can mechanically catch a half-done rename" and told the next patrol to read its CI conclusion before arming. **That is false.** `lychee.toml` sets `include_fragments = "none"`, and the dev did not take that from the config comment — it **probed the pinned lychee 0.24.2 under the CI argv** with a link to `…#this-anchor-does-not-exist-at-all` and got `[200] ✅ OK`. The gate resolves the **file** target only.

So **no CI gate in this repo checks documentation anchors**. What actually verifies this rename is (a) the slug computed with the repo's own `github-slugger@2.0.0` — `slug("The one gate, four doors")` → `the-one-gate-four-doors` — and (b) the repo-wide grep showing no residual references. Both were done. Filing the gap separately; ⛔ not riding it onto this PR.

## Out-of-surface drift, correctly left alone

The stale `26` also survives in two **code comments** — `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:76` and `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:2542`. Outside this card's file surface and outside its docs-only shape. Recorded in the PR body and being filed, rather than widened into this diff.
